shared_elements: monolithic block of coarse stone as the carrying surface
shallow low-relief carving with rounded, softened edges
curvilinear/abstract motifs rather than naturalistic scenes
a ring or circular disc motif
band-like horizontal element crossing the face
justification: Both are vertical stone monoliths bearing very shallow, weathered relief of curvilinear, non-naturalistic motifs, and each includes a ring/disc form and a band-like element crossing a broad flat face, which is the most specific correspondence. The biggest difference is scope and form: A is a cropped detail of an unmodelled rectangular pillar edge amid rubble, while B is a complete anthropomorphic figure with head and shoulders whose ornament is organised symmetrically around the body, so the compositional logic cannot be shown to match.
